subject: Hosted API p95 degradation — initial notice and immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Aria Patel <aria@lumensys.com>, support@lumensys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p95 degradation — initial notice and immediate mitigation plan

Hi Aria,

We observed an elevated p95 response time for your account's hosted inference traffic (region: us-west-1) beginning ~14:42 PDT. Our automated detection flagged a sustained p95 of ~1.8s (baseline ~0.6s) for generation requests using the pinned model. This is affecting a subset of tokens for streaming responses and causing visible latency spikes in your staging environment.

Immediate actions we've taken: 
- Activated a temporary routing policy to shift new requests to a healthy capacity pool in us-west-2 (should reduce impact for new sessions).
- Increased KV cache retention for your tenant's prefix to reduce token recomputation.
- Opened internal incident INC-20270720-1782; eng on-call is triaging root cause.

Why you might have noticed errors: some in-flight streaming sessions saw elongation/fragmentation which produced delayed chunking to clients. We've observed this mainly for requests with long context windows (>2k tokens).

What we need from you (short list):
- Can you confirm whether you see user-facing errors or primarily slow responses?
- If possible, please share any request IDs or example sessions where you saw the worst latency so we can correlate.

We'll share continuous updates on the status page link and aim for a full remediation or a durable workaround within the next 4 hours. I'm looping Marissa and Evelyn for tracking and RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with high priority.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: lumensys_tail_logs.txt (text log excerpt)

Thanks Marcus — we are seeing severe slowdowns on a small percentage (~3-4%) of production calls; clients report timeouts (30s) rather than errors. User-facing issue is more about latency/timeouts, not incorrect outputs.

Included below are two request IDs from our logs where the UI froze: req_20270720_aa1 and req_20270720_aa2. Those correspond to long-assisted writing flows (context ~3.5k tokens).

Please confirm what compensating controls we should enable on our side (smaller chunk size? retry window?). Also — can you advise whether this qualifies for SLA credit consideration; we'd like to understand potential remediation steps on a billing/contract level.

- Telemetry shows increased kernel queue latency correlated with background KV eviction for some pools.

Subject: Update: mitigation active and next steps (post-incident follow-up meeting invite)

Hi Aria — quick update and plan: 

What we found so far:
- Root cause (preliminary): synchronized KV cache eviction across a subset of us-west-1 serving nodes during a burst of long-context requests. That produced correlated cache misses and a transient p95 elevation.
- Impact window: 2027-07-20T14:42:00-07:00 to 2027-07-20T15:10:00-07:00 for the majority of affected sessions. A small tail persisted for ~40 minutes.

What we did:
- Rerouted new traffic to us-west-2 for reduced latency while we patched the eviction scheduling.
- Adjusted eviction schedule to de-synchronize across pools and increased soft-cache thresholds for long-context tenants.
- Pushed a hotfix that reduces synchronous recompute on cache misses for streaming sessions (deployed 2027-07-20T19:08:00Z).

Customer-facing credits and next steps: 
- We will evaluate SLA credit eligibility for impacted billable tokens during the impact window. I'll coordinate with Billing and share an itemized credit calculation by Fri 2027-07-23.
- We're scheduling a 45-minute post-incident review with you on Thu 2027-07-22 10:00 AM PDT to walk through the timeline, technical root cause, and hardening roadmap. Calendar invite attached.

Attachments: incidental_sla_matrix.pdf (proposed credit worksheet)
Status page: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incident/2027-07-hosted-degrade-1782
